conventions.convention: The primal maximizes tr(CX) under X ≥ 0 and tr(A_jX) ≤ b_j; the dual minimizes b·y under y ≥ 0 and sum_j y_j A_j − C ≥ 0. Feasibility, attainment and bounded optimal multipliers are separate promises.
Root complex inner products are linear in the first argument; Dirac expectations use the reversed pairing.
MMW uses W_t = exp(−η sum_{s<t} M_s), normalized by its trace, with Hermitian losses between −I and I and 0 < η ≤ 1.
Successful amplification measures only the supplied good/bad flag and preserves the normalized good projection up to global phase; score, label and work registers remain unmeasured.
The reference is the maximally entangled state on the original d labels. General-dimension preparation and its inverse are supplied and charged; padding must account for its trace effects.
The energy shift is measured once and frozen before indexed trace circuits. Numerator and baseline use the same Gibbs and observable normalizations; the baseline observable block is I/(2 B_A^+).
Weak membership has a fixed deterministic completion in its boundary overlap. Weak separation emits an outward unit normal with an upper halfspace inequality on the inward erosion.
Countable choice is assumed for the volume-based centroid optimization reduction; exhaustive exact centroid arithmetic is charged separately and has no asserted polynomial bit-time bound.
QAOA applies the cost factor before the mixer in each round, with cost sum_edges (I − Z_u Z_v)/2 and mixer sum_vertices X_v.

load_bearing.statement: For the finite capped sampler, with probability at least 1−δ the returned score v satisfies Pr(score < v) < 1/N. Its coherent-score version, under the stated preserved-index and bad-label bounds, returns a good label whose score is not strictly greater than every good label at any one index.

Under its frozen-G, common-normalization, block-error and access hypotheses, the clipped ratio estimate approximates tr(Aρ_G) within θ on the joint relative-estimation good event. Actual flag probabilities exceed 1/(1024d), and complete primitive access count is Õ(√d/θ), with additional operations separately charged.

On the joint good event of the two supplied robust minima, the finite planar procedure returns a nonnegative rational vector with at most two nonzero coordinates, norm at most r, objective at most α and true trace residual at least −2(r+1)θ, or EMPTY implying α < v_D.
For n,T ≥ 1, 0 < η ≤ 1 and Hermitian losses −I ≤ M_t ≤ I, sum_t tr(M_tρ_t) ≤ λ_min(sum_t M_t) + ηT + ln(n)/η.

For the normalized Hermitian inequality SDP with A_1=I, b_1=R>0, norm bounds at most one and nonempty primal, the primal feasible set is compact, its maximum is attained, and p*=d* ∈ [−R,R]. Dual optimal attainment remains a separate promise.

Under its normalized SDP promises and specified parameters, every good threshold execution either returns EMPTY implying α<v, or returns a feasible averaged dual with matrix slack at least (e/(2R))I and objective at most α+e.

Under the stated absolutely convergent Taylor coefficient budget, its finite arcsine convolution and binomial truncations give uniform error below e/8 with exact coefficient norm at most B; total coefficient rounding error at most e/16 gives error below e/4 and norm at most B+e/16.

Under its convexity, local Lipschitz, bounded-subgradient and clean deterministic value-oracle hypotheses, the finite-grid procedure returns, with probability at least 1−ρ, v satisfying f(y) ≥ f(0)+⟨v,y⟩−(23n)^2√(δL/(ρ₀r₁))‖y‖−2L√n r₁ simultaneously for every y in C, using O(log(n/ρ)) value-oracle and inverse calls.

Under countable choice and its radius, precision and normal-encoding hypotheses, the finite classical reduction uses at most BT = O(n log(nR/s)(1+log(R/ζ))) weak-separation calls and returns, with probability at least 1−ν, y ∈ B(K,ζ) with objective at least max_K⟨c,x⟩−ζ.

concerns.concern: The final Statement claims that if h(y) ≥ h(0)+⟨v,y⟩−a‖y‖−b on C, then the normalized separator obeys ⟨s,z⟩ ≥ ⟨s,x⟩−aR−b−2Rε/r, but imposes no nonnegativity condition on a. Counterexample: n=2, K=[−1,1]^2, r=1, R=2, ε=1/100, x=(0,−1), v=0, a=−1 and b=1. Here C=[−1,1], h(y)=−1, and the premise is −1 ≥ −2+|y|, valid throughout C. OUT at x is a valid weak-membership answer because x is not in the ε-erosion. The prescribed s=(0,1) and z=(0,−1) give left side −1, whereas the claimed right side is −1/25. Proof 6.1 uses −a‖y‖ ≥ −aR, which requires a ≥ 0. The consuming membership-separation theorem supplies positive error coefficients, but the lemma's unrestricted claim is false as written.

seams_checked.note: Preserves the eigenstate qualification; repeated coherent trials share one preserved spectral index. The chosen QPE schedule is justified directly rather than inferred from a different least-size schedule.
Uses the bounded-observable estimator with supplied coherent sampler, inverse and controls; repeated-call and supplied-power costs remain distinct.
Dirac expectations consistently reverse the root linear-first pairing.
POVM outcome weights are distinguished from state updates; amplification explicitly supplies a flag-only branch instrument.
Density operators have nonzero finite-dimensional spaces and trace one; coherent purification access is supplied separately.
No channel representation is treated as a free circuit or as controlled access.
Chronological products and retained orthogonal measurement histories agree with the finite circuit conventions; implementations and costs are explicit.
Controlled and inverse access remain separate capabilities. The local Grover sign is explicitly specified.
Ordered reference factors and original-label traces are retained; zero qubits are distinguished from zero-dimensional spaces.
Matrix-query counts do not imply uniform generation or total gate bounds; description, arithmetic, memory and preparation costs remain charged.
Uses total completed XOR oracles and explicit retained history or compute-copy-uncompute; no inverse follows from postselection.
Relative estimation retains its positive floor, finite cap, confidence budget and separately supplied controlled reflections and samplers.
Uses the generic relative-probability procedure with its declared rounding mode and complete-circuit inverse; no normalized conditional-state inverse is inferred.
LCU normalization, separate work registers and supplied PREPARE/SELECT costs are preserved; compressions are not treated as unitaries.
Finite spectral evolutions define mathematical operators; implementation access and simulation costs are supplied independently.
The gradient procedure uses the negative-sign inverse of the supplier's positive-sign QFT.
Uses circular phase tails and signed principal decoding, retaining the distinction between power-evolution time and repeated base calls.
Sorted XOR access pays its location overhead and permits listed zeros. Simulation errors are composed on clean input subspaces, including inverses and references.
Uses the stated Pauli signs and exp(−iθP/2) rotation convention.
The example's computational-basis probabilities are squared amplitudes and sum to one.
The Ry product-state energy and one-edge QAOA output use the supplier's exact rotation signs and phases.
